content.user_title: Review and Simplify Code Without Losing Correctness
content.value_statement: Complex logic and unnecessary abstractions make code harder to maintain and can hide failures. This skill guides focused reviews and refactors that preserve behavior, public contracts, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Guide input tracing through validation, decisions, and side effects to identify coupled responsibilities and hidden failures.
Evaluate branch, abstraction, and dependency removal using callers, tests, public contracts, and maintenance cost.
Review boundary cases involving missing inputs, duplicates, concurrency, retries, cancellation, and partial writes.
Check sensitive paths for authorization, contextual output encoding, safe query and command APIs, and secret-free logging.
Guide behavior-level verification and reports with actionable findings, concrete locations, validation results, and remaining tradeoffs.
limitations: Provides written guidance, not an executable analyzer or bundled test suite.
Requires relevant code, callers, and tests to support reliable review conclusions.
Cannot guarantee correctness; validation depends on available tools, tests, and execution access.
Does not replace a security-specific review or prescribe a universal response format.

use_cases.title: Review a Feature Change
use_cases.description: Check changed code for failure paths, boundary conditions, and broken public contracts before merging.

use_cases.title: Simplify Legacy Logic
use_cases.description: Trace tangled behavior and remove unnecessary branches or indirection only when callers and tests justify the change.

use_cases.title: Investigate Asynchronous Failures
use_cases.description: Review state ownership, retries, cancellation, and partial writes to identify inconsistent transitions and meaningful regression tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [function or file] for correctness and readability. Trace one representative input and report actionable findings with consequences and locations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a focused review of a small code section.

prompt_templates.title: Simplify a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Simplify [module] while preserving its public contract and error behavior. Check callers, use existing repository conventions, and validate changed behavior with relevant tests.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Dependency Removal
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate removing [dependency or abstraction]. Identify callers, compare replacement behavior and maintenance cost, and propose a focused patch only when evidence supports removal.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: evidence-based dependency or abstraction cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrent State Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [workflow] for retries, cancellation, stale results, and partial writes. Trace state transitions, preserve security checks, and reproduce failures before proposing tested fixes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: correctness review of asynchronous or concurrent behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a search workflow where an earlier request can complete after a later request.
output: Finding: an older response can overwrite the current search results.
Consequence: users can see results that do not match their latest query.
Recommendation: accept results only when they belong to the current request.
Validation: test responses completing in reverse order and cancellation during an active request.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a wrapper around a standard parser can be removed.
output: Check callers for custom defaults, error handling, and compatibility requirements before removing the wrapper.
Replace the wrapper only when the standard parser preserves the required behavior.
Validate empty inputs, malformed inputs, and failure contracts.
Keep the wrapper when it represents a real ownership or compatibility boundary.

best_practices: Provide the requested change, relevant callers, public contracts, and existing tests before starting a review.
Reproduce reported failures when feasible and validate meaningful failure paths after making changes.
Keep changes focused and preserve security checks, accessibility, compatibility, and error recovery.
anti_patterns: Treating a smaller line count as proof of correctness or maintainability.
Removing abstractions or dependencies without checking callers and behavior contracts.
Combining unrelated cleanup with a focused fix or compressing readable logic into clever expressions.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it for requested code reviews, refactors, dependency cleanup, or investigation of tangled logic. It is not a default checklist for every small edit.

faq.question: Does this skill include an automated analyzer?
faq.answer: No. It contains review and simplification instructions, with no executable analyzer or bundled scripts.

faq.question: Will it always remove abstractions?
faq.answer: No. It preserves abstractions that express real boundaries, ownership rules, testing needs, or variation.

faq.question: How does it handle testing?
faq.answer: It guides appropriate checks, failure reproduction when feasible, and behavior-level tests covering meaningful failure paths.

faq.question: Can it replace a dedicated security review?
faq.answer: No. It includes sensitive-path checks but directs security-focused work to a security-specific review.

faq.question: Does it require a fixed report format?
faq.answer: No. Reviews prioritize actionable findings with consequences and locations. Edit reports summarize simplification, preserved behavior, validation, and remaining tradeoffs.
